title: Photography
text:
As a wizard and scholar of Middle-earth, I have been studying the magic of the natural world for centuries. Through my self-portraits, I aim to capture the essence of my own being and reflect on my own journey through time. Each photograph is a reflection of my own experiences and emotions. Through my photography, I hope to offer a glimpse into my life as a scholar and adventurer, and inspire others to reflect on their own journeys through the world.

title: Projects
text:
arXiv Preprint | Code
Over the centuries, I have devoted countless hours to deciphering and translating the ancient scripts and dialects of the various peoples of Middle-earth. My goal is to gain a deeper understanding of the cultures and histories of these peoples by studying their languages. Currently, I am working on a monograph that explores the linguistic roots of the Elvish languages. Through extensive research and analysis, I hope to shed light on the connections between the different dialects of Elvish and their origins. This project has been particularly challenging, as Elvish is a complex and nuanced language, but I am determined to see it through to completion.

Welcome to my website!
Salutations! My name is Namjun Cho, and I am a PhD candidate in Biomedical Engineering at Case Western Reserve University (CWRU). I earned my Bachelor’s of Science in Bioengineering from the beautiful campus of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 2025. There, I first sparked my interest in research under Dr. Jia Dong and Dr. Matthew Hudson by aiding their efforts in protoplast isolation, protoplast transformation, and enhancing lipid production in maize, sorghum, and N. Benthamiana. From there, I diversified my experience by joining Dr. Min Jee Jang’s lab, supporting the newly established lab with neuronal cell culture, calcium imaging, optogenetics, and confocal microscopy, as well as learning about AAV production and spatial transcriptomics. Throughout my degree, I completed rigorous coursework in the therapeutics track and finished the degree with a senior design project on transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation for individuals with Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome. (POTS).
Here at CWRU, I am in Dr. Mei Zhang’s lab studying fungal biology and immunoengineering for the ultimate goal of enabling microbiome-based therapeutic strategies. As part of my training, I am supporting benchtop and clinical research for our established CD11b-targeting therapy, which promotes differentiation of monocytes into dendritic cells. In parallel, I am employing fungal biology, neuronal cell culture, and protein-based signaling analyses to understand how commensal skin fungi contribute to the skin-brain axis. I am currently learning many hard and soft skills, including fungal and neuronal cell culture, Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated gene transfer (ATMT), yeast-to-hyphal induction, mass spectrometry (MS), good manufacturing practices (GMP), and many more.
Please feel free to contact me if you would like to chat, collaborate, or just want to comment. All is welcome!

title: Labor and Delivery Dashboard
text:
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(scales)
library(DT)
library(gt)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 24, base_family = "sans"))
ld <- read_excel("data/ld.xlsx")
time_period <- paste(params$month, params$year)
ld <- ld |>
  mutate(
    delivery_method = str_to_sentence(delivery_method),
    term = str_to_sentence(term),
    parity = case_when(
      parity == "1"  ~ "Nulliparous",
      parity == "2"  ~ "Primiparous",
      parity == "3+" ~ "Multiparous"
    ),
    parity = fct_relevel(parity, "Nulliparous", "Primiparous", "Multiparous"),
    maternal_age = fct_relevel(maternal_age, "<20", "20-34", "35+")
  )

  count(parity, delivery_method) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = fct_rev(parity), fill = delivery_method)) +

    values = c("#ae8b2d", "#0e2635"),
    guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL, fill = "Delivery\nmethod")

title: Labor and Delivery Dashboard
text:
Column

ld_v <- ld |>
  filter(delivery_method == "Vaginal")

n_births_v <- nrow(ld_v)

p_preterm_v <- ld_v |>
  count(term) |>
  mutate(p = n / sum(n)) |>
  filter(term == "Pre-term") |>
  pull(p)

p_preterm_color_v <- case_when(
  between(p_preterm_v, params$us_preterm_rate, params$us_preterm_rate + params$threshold_diff) ~ "warning",
  p_preterm_v > params$us_preterm_rate + params$threshold_diff ~ "danger",
  .default = "light"
  )
